author: RUTHINAS
content:
Yes. I started at level 34, but it probably would have worked even earlier. Importantly it was well before any of the tanking tools added by Turtle. Outdamaging your party is your aggro, so it's quite dependent on gear. Leveling as Slow & Steady tends to help, since your levels don't keep up with your gear progression. I would consider engineering as pretty much a necessity; grenades give you a lot of area threat and survivability, target dummies can be used to taunt mobs off squishy party members, and spell reflectors help a ton with key caster mobs.

Some level 60 dungeons will be extremely tricky due to recent changes making specific elemental mobs immune to poisons, Dire Maul: West being one of the more frustrating examples. Also, lacking a taunt there are several raid bosses that can not be feasibly tanked by rogues (but on the other hand some, where the taunt mechanic is not a necessary consideration if the boss is tanked by a rogue, so look out for those). However, despite these difficulties and certain nerfs, rogues maintain a certain viability even into raid content. It is however rather difficult to get most guilds to diverge from the warrior tank status quo, even if for some encounters rogues are clearly the better choice.

As a final tip I recommend you unlearn the need to build large combos. As a tank your task is to maintain threat on multiple targets, meaning that sticking to building combos will prevent target swaps to a detrimental degree. I recommend building one or two combo points, casting slice and dice (if it needs refreshing) and moving to the next target. 5-combo eviscerates are not something you will be doing outside of single target boss encounters.

content:
**Leveling talents**
[Updated September 16th 2025]
The reworked talent trees are all suited for leveling up, although builds based around Backstab, and builds centered around the Subtlety tree, are more suited for group leveling. There is a technique called 'frontstabbing' that allows for the use of Backstab even in solo content, but it can be a bit unwieldy.

I'd argue that there is no "ideal" leveling build, as it all comes down to preference. However, some individual talents are more valuable for leveling up than others.

Improved Gouge is a literal lifesaver in a multitude of situations, but its greatest value comes from allowing one to bandage during combat (against a single target, or against two if you're able to use Blind or Kidney Shot on the other, or even three if you use all of the aforementioned abilities, though you will need to pay attention to your energy pool).

Lightning Reflexes and Deflection both improve your survivability by a fair amount, and they synergise well with Riposte and Setup, converting avoidance into damage output. They're less beneficial if you are leveling up with a tank, but don't be afraid to tank yourself; rogues _can_ tank all instances in the game if one so desires.

Improved Dual Wield is one of the greatest damage increasing talents, and Precision both improves your damage output and makes hitting important abilities more reliable (imagine missing that lifesaving Gouge!), so getting them is of key importance if heading down the Combat tree.

Ruthlessness has been changed to provide a 100% chance of retaining a combo point after using a finisher, which can also be used to "drift" a combo point to another target: certain finishers can be used even if you are not currently targeting the enemy which your combo is built on, and by doing so the extra combo point is transferred to your new target.

Improved Blade Tactics is fantastic as well, and so is Relentless Strikes.

Improved Ambush can be used to deal immense opener damage.

author: RUTHINAS
content: The build works great at 60 too, but for raiding I would recommend making some changes. If you wish to keep using swords, fist weapons, maces (or axes in the upcoming patch) then this build is very strong. You can move the points around a little bit depending on preference. Deflection is better than Lightning Reflexes because parries increase the attack speed of your next swing. Improved Sprint or Endurance are both great talents but I prefer being able to remove roots and slows. You can have both if you give up two points from Deflection, or if you use maces and have no need for Weapon Expertise. Murder is wasted talents against mob types not listed, and you can move the points to Improved Poisons for instance.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
The basic idea of rogue gameplay is maintaining Slice and Dice constantly. It is your most powerful ability. After your opener it would be ideal to cast it as soon as you are able to (usually at one or two combo points) and refreshing it when it is about to run out. While the buff will last longer per combo point, gaining those combo points costs energy. Using the finisher at low combo points will be more economical in terms of energy expenditure, but will give you a shorter window to do other things. Find a balance that fits the situation best.

You may sometimes get a chance to use other finishers too; if the target will stay alive long enough for the damage over time effect to run its course, Rupture is a solid alternative to Eviscerate, but if the enemy is close to death you will want to hit Eviscerate instead. If you need to, you can Kidney Shot a mob to reduce the pressure on the tank(s) and healer(s), but be aware that many raid mobs will be immune to it. You can and should use Flourish to increase your parry chance when mobs turn to attack you, or if you are fighting mobs with multi-target melee abilities like Whirlwind or area knockbacks. Any damage you don't take is mana a healer does not need to spend!

If you already have some hit gear, 4/5 Precision should be fine. Otherwise I would swap one point from Serrated Blades to get it to 5/5.

For PvE, Improved Poisons is stronger than Vile Poisons; if using Instant Poison with a baseline 20% proc rate, upping the proc rate to 30% is equivalent to increasing damage by 50% (as opposed to 20% gained from Vile Poisons). For Deadly the difference is not as great as further applications beyond 5 stacks don't have an effect on the damage, but you would be able to get the stacks up 33% faster (Deadly Poison baseline proc rate is 30%; bringing it to 40% is a 33% increase). On longer fights, if you do use Deadly Poison, I suggest swapping to 2/3 Improved Poisons and 3/3 Vile Poisons as that would lead to more damage from the 5-stack.

Improved Poisons also helps with fishing for Vigor procs, especially since you elected not to put two points in it. Lacking Envenom the 50% chance will be a noticeable downgrade from 100%, so keep this in mind.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
This would probably serve you quite well as a Combat-centered dagger leveling build:

Start with **Improved Gouge**, then go for **2/5 Lightning Reflexes** to reach the second row of talents. Pick up **Precision** first, then **Blade Flurry**, only then backtrack to get **Improved Backstab**.

At this point, you can optionally pick up **Remorseless Attacks** from the Assassination tree if you tend to play solo, but for dungeon leveling you can skip it and move directly over to Subtlety for **Opportunity** and **Improved Ambush**.

After this, select a talent point of your choice in the Combat tree (my preference is **1/5 Deflection** for extra avoidance, as parry is slightly stronger than dodge due to "parry haste" which makes your next attack connect faster after parrying) to unlock the next row and take **Dual Wield Specialization**, then **Blade Rush** and **Close Quarters Combat**.

Then, dedicate your final points into the Assassination tree. Take **Malice**, follow up with **Ruthlessness** and **Improved Blade Tactics** to more easily maintain your Slice and Dice buff, and finish off with **Relentless Strikes** and **Lethality**.

If you did not pick up Remorseless Attacks, the final two points are free-form in placement. I feel like **Improved Sprint** has saved my skin quite often. To get the most out of it, you can pick it up earlier rather than later.

Alternative talent strategies exist too, so feel free to experiment. Serrated Blades is a great talent in the Subtlety tree, Surprise Attack grants some really solid combo generation, and is followed by Weapon Expertise for a strong source of dagger skill, to name a few examples.

Ultimately you will want to respec out of this leveling build at 60, but this should get you there with relative ease. Since Ambush is heavily emphasized, you will not have to "frontstab" as much (which is admittedly not a playstyle for everyone – certainly not for me at the very least).

Enjoy, and good luck!

author: RUTHINAS
content:
A quite typical Combat/Assassination leveling build works very well. Damage is threat, so pick up what you need to maintain aggro, while getting avoidance talents, Riposte, Blade Flurry (very good for multi-target threat, but I recommend engineering grenades additionally).

Setup gives you a fair bit of combo points for all sorts of valuable utility, but losing your combo to generate threat on other targets is typical; while most of your threat comes from auto-attacks in one way or another, abilities can provide good burst threat when someone else is stealing aggro.

Adrenaline Rush is a great threat cooldown, but the extra energy can be converted into avoidance and utility abilities too. After getting it I would shift my focus to Assassination for Ruthlessness (which is honestly good enough to warrant picking up earlier too, maybe after Blade Flurry?), Improved Blade Tactics and and Relentless Strikes.

At 60 you can supplement your build with Improved Poisons for better Agitating Poison threat, or you can change to a dedicated poisoner build with Envenom for fantastic threat and a fairly interesting gameplay of using lots of low-combo finishers, keeping track of specific timings.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
Don't be afraid to put more than 31 points in the Subtlety tree. Maxing out both Tricks of the Trade and Honor Among Thieves _is_ worth it. I would personally go for Assassination talents over Combat, since Improved Expose Armor is a great debuff that will further amplify your capacity to increase the raid's physical damage output.

Here's a quick mock-up build. There is a bunch of flexibility in the talent points here, and you are left with 4 extra points to apply wherever you feel they would provide the most value. Murder is great for targets its effect applies to but useless otherwise. Improved Poisons or Vile Poisons can be used to increase your poison damage (Vile is better if you have enough attack power for it to outscale the extra damage provided by additional procs), or alternatively you can go for Dirty Deeds to make your opener-to-finisher pipeline faster; start with Garrote or Cheap Shot for initial combo points (+1 from Initiative), use Hemorrhage to build up to 5 and use Expose Armor as a finisher. This way you will drop the target's armor very quickly, but also apply two stacks of Tricks of the Trade to your party. If you have proc-based effects that you rely on (such as Darkmantle set bonus), Swift Strikes can be used to gain an increased benefit from them.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
You can skip Aggression and Swift Strikes while leveling up. It should also be said that avoidance talents are the most valuable when you are doing solo leveling (or tanking, but that's not for the faint of heart), so if you run a lot of dungeons you can skip Lightning Reflexes, Deflection, Riposte and Setup altogether (using them only to advance to later talent tiers). Improved Gouge is also really good for leveling up, as it allows you to bandage mid-combat for longer.

Essentially I would recommend you to get to Adrenaline Rush at level 40 and then moving over to the Assassination tree, but there are many schools of thought here. Some swear by Remorseless Attacks and pick it with their first two talent points, and only then head down Combat, but personally I prefer to spend those points elsewhere.

This is what I would build towards personally, if I were to level up a new rogue as Combat. The remaining 8 points can be distributed quite freely; going for Serrated Blades from Subtlety is a valid choice, as is heading deeper into Assassination for Murder and/or Lethality and poison talents, or Improved Expose Armor if you want to play the armor reducer role in raids. Alternatively you can pick up more Lightning Reflexes and Setup if you're doing solo content or tanking, Aggression for a bit of extra damage, or utility talents of your choice (Improved Sprint is great, Improved Kick has its uses in PvP and PvE alike). Certain Eviscerate builds would pick up Aggression and Improved Eviscerate, and so on.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
Yes. Leveling up you will want to look at a Combat/Assassination build with avoidance talents, and at 60 you can lean deep into the Assassination tree for Envenom, which couples extremely well with your Agitating Poison, a poison that generates bonus threat with each proc.

Your damage is your threat during the leveling process, so pick talents and gear accordingly. You should be able to keep threat quite well however, at least once you get to Blade Flurry in the Combat tree, allowing you to damage two targets simultaneously. Engineering helps _a lot_ for multi-target fights, both grenades and target dummies are indispensable.

```I think the devs did a great job with the poison changes recently.  It's my opinion that Assassination Daggers is the class / spec with the most room for a skill ceiling in the game.  

With between 1-3 combos per backstab, you can't predict the best rotation possible but have to make choices on the fly.  

We also have energy vs combo points vs time on boss / buffs, which is a fun puzzle to try to optimize in real time.

Rogues also have thistle tea which is used optimall when a GCD is available and you reached exactly 0 energy.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
In terms of buff duration / energy cost, it is _cheaper_ to use Slice and Dice & Envenom & Taste of Blood Rupture at the smallest possible combo point value. The largest expense is building the combo points in the first place, and the duration provided by the first combo point is longer than the additional duration granted by each point beyond the first.

Regardless of my opening move I always follow up with a Slice and Dice right after, and Envenom next by using the combo point provided by Ruthlessness, then Rupture on the target for Taste for Blood to activate. When any of the three buffs is about to fall off, I refresh it as close to 0 seconds as possible, regardless of my current combo point situation. Any time not spent refreshing the trio is spent dealing damage with Sinister Strike (in my case).

author: RUTHINAS
content: Leveling up you will not have access to Agitating Poison, meaning that your only option for threat is dealing raw damage. Any damage dealing build will work as long as you can generate more threat than your party members, but the Combat tree also provides a fair bit of avoidance (and additional avoidance-based threat through Riposte and Setup) and Blade Flurry for tanking multiple targets. Something along these lines would be my recommended leveling build, but you can shift points around to pick up utility talents (Improved Kick, Improved Sprint are both great for tanks). I pick Improved Gouge for leveling up, but you can move the points over to Lightning Reflexes if you so wish.

author: RUTHINAS
content: At 60 you can look into a more single-target focused threat build with the acquisition of Agitating Poison. Vile Poisons may not be necessary (it increases only the damage portion of Agitating Poison, not the bonus threat – and said poison does not scale with Attack Power) and can possibly be replaced by Improved Eviscerate, some more points in Seal Fate, Improved Expose Armor. Murder also becomes unnecessary in some content, allowing those two talent points to be freed up for other uses, but you would want to take it for content where it matters.

author: Eylo
content:
Horde or Alli?
PVP or PvE?
Daggers or Swords/Axes or Support?

**Alliance:**

- **Human**: Best for sword rogue, since they get +3 on expertise  and can be support. You get crit chance and stealth detection in PvP, it's niche, but useful against rogues and undeads. Balanced choice. 
**PvE**: 5/5 
**PvP**: 3/5

- **Dwarf**: One of the best, if not the best PvP rogue. Stoneform removes bleeds, dieases, poisons (Blind is a poison) + extra tankines. It's technically a semi-Cloak of Shadow On PvE you don't get anything, just choose Assa or Combat Daggers to get daggers, so you can PvP more effectively.
**PvE**: 0/5
**PvP**: 5/5

- **Night Elf**: Combat Daggers/Assassination. You gain 1% attack speed, movement speed, dodge chance + highest starting Agi! Additonally you gain +1 stealth level. Racial is useless, but can be used, if stealth is on cd to get away. Not a good choice for PvP, but better, than human, if you ask me.
**PvE**: 5/5
**PvP**: 3/5

- **Gnome**: Has the 2nd best starting Agi in the alliance. You get a really nice racial, which removes movement imparing effects. Suitable for PvP. I would say go for daggers or if you really want to PvP with Swords with Hemo build.
**PVE**: 2/5
**PvP**: 5/5

- **High Elf**: They have medicore starting agility. They gain 2% agi, which scales well, but worse than Night Elf, but with like 1-2 dps.. You also gain an okay racial, which gives you 50 energy. This one is useful for Assa and combat dagger/support rogues. Worst race for PvP.
**PvE**: 5/5
**PvP**: 0/5

author: Eylo
content:
**Horde:**

- **Orc**: Stun resist was changed into lower durration, which is still really really useful in PvP. They get a really good bursty racial. They are most suitable for combat axe rogue, since rogue can wield axes in TWoW.  Orcs get +3 on axe expertise. Really balanced pick, if you ask me.
**PvE**: 5/5
**PvP**: 4/5

- **Undead**: Will of the Forsaken is nice, but i have to remind everyone in here. Priests are not a problem. Good against warrior's fear shout. Nice gainst warlocks, but they once again shouldn't cause any issue, if you are geared or skilled enough. They gain 2% damage agains humanoids and undead (Non-player). Canibalism is underrated in PvP, especially on bgs.
**PvE**: 1/5
**PvP**: 4/5

- **Troll**: You get high starting agility and really awesome racial, which increases your attack speed. Nice pick, if you wanna be support/assassination/combat dagger rogue. Decent in PvP.
**PvE**: 3/5
**PvP**: 2/5

- **Goblin**: Most suitable for Dagger and Assassinations rogues, since you get +3 for expertise. On top of that you get a free sprint, which is really nice to use it as a gap closer against ranged or to kite those pesky warriors outside of charge range. Decent for both content. I would choocse it over undead for pvp.
**PvE**: 5/5
**PvP**: 4/5

author: Eylo
content: Rogue doesn't have a rottation. Depends on what you are up against. You always need to be one step ahead! Know what your opponent will react to your response. Think about it like it's a chess. Utilize stuns: Cheap Shot, Gouge, Kidney shot. Build your combo points with Hemo/BS, then use Evi, Vanish can be used as a defensive tool or as an offensive tool. Mind you we do not have a cloak of shadow! Dwarf's stoneform is your best bet and really strong. You can kite melee out of melee range with crippling poison. Warrior is the best example here. They aren't gonna be able to charge you, if you stay in melee range in combat. Orcs are no longer have stun ressist, but durration reduction as their passive, which means you have to count with it, if you are facing em. The reason why we do not use stacking poisons such as deadly poison is becuz we need to gouge and blind.

Race rankings for pvp:
- Dwarf: Stone form is a Cloak of Shadow, but doesn't remove magical effects. On the other hand Blind is a poison status effect.
- Gnome: Removing any movement imparing effect is good, like frost novas, concusive shot, crippling poison, etc.. Especially nice on bgs. Pretacullary on WSG, in case you don't have a feral druid with extra movement speed talent (I dunno, if they changed it or not)

content:
Gonna teach ya how to be the **ass as ssin**:
- 1 CP SnD
- 1 CP Envenom
- 5 CP Rupture (Taste for Blood), if Rupture doesn't apply, becuz the boss dodges, parries whatever you can use 5 CP Eviserate
- Refres 1 CP Envenom 1 CP SnD
- 5 CP Evi, if you can have 100% uptime on the boss and there're no move out mechanics, if there are, then upkeep 5 CP Rupture
- Repeat

- Cold Blood is only used, when you don't crit with Noxius Assault, so you have 3 CP, it will allow you to have 5 CP Rupture to utilze Taste for Blood
- Venomous Totem used, after you have 5 CP Rupture aka Taste for Blood, so Disolvent Poison can benifit from it
- Trinket swap, after you used Venmous totem or whatever trinket, vanish and trinket swap
- Dynamites not worth using, unlike Holywater, cuz you'll lose more dps in the process, since it has cast time
- Living Action Potion: Worth using over a vanish. Why? It allows you to trinket swap, whenever you draw aggro, like bwl rogue class call  can happen and you have to Vanish (becuz we dont use Imp Sprint  talent)

author: Rheinwg
content:
What poisons should i use on each raid?

Before we start: 

- Every spec with envenom should be using dissolvent/instant (Edit: Apparently Deadly and Cor are actually pretty good for Combat envenom) 
- Meanwhile Combat and Sub should change from instant poisons to dot poisons depending on the length of the fight, usually if the fight is over 40s long is better to use dot poisons, if is shorter you have to use instant/dissolvent.

Molten Core: 

- Trash:  The entirety of Molten Core is filled with different kind of enemies, but the most usual ones are Elementals and Giants. For this reason is recommended to use Dissolvent poison 2 for most of the trash, just put the Core Hounds on low priority. The only exception is the section with a green line where you should use Instant poison

- Bosses: Garr, Geddon, the Two Golems and the Undead Dwarf can only be damaged by Dissolvent or Corrosive.  The Salamander, the Core Hound, Sulfuron, Shazzrah and Mayordmo can only be damaged with Instant and Deadly. Golemagg is a giant and can be damage by both kind of poisons.

On the image: Orange is dissolvent and corrosive, green is instant and deadly

author: Rheinwg
content:
Naxxramas:

- Trash: Since most of the raid is composed of undead you are safe to use both kind of poisons. But there are several humanoids and beast around the instance, making instant the easier pick to be able to damage everyone.

- Bosses: most of bosses can be hurt with both kind of poisons, with the exception of Faerlina, Maexxna, and Gothik. Assa can run with either diss or instant, meanwhile combat and sub should be using Deadly 5 and Corrosive 2 on most bosses, and using Deadly 5 + Deadly 4 on Faerlina and Maexxa. Gothik is only dissolvent.

On the image: green path is for instant, 2 color X is for both kind of poisons, green x is for Deadly/instant only.

Red is red because i forgot the trash was also undead.

author: Rheinwg
content:
Tower of Karazhan:
On trash:

- The entire tower is filled with mixed enemies, pick your poison (lol) and stick to it, prio the enemies you can hurt.
- Before Gnarlmoon you face Humanoids, Beast and Undeads. Use instant
- Between Gnarlmoon and Incantagos you can only find Dragons, use instant
- Between Incantagos and Anomalus the packs are Dragons and elementals, pick a posion.
- After Anomalus most of the enemies are undead, elementals or mechanicals, use dissolvent
- After Chess you gonna find Undeads, and right after that pack all of the enemies are either humanoids or demons. Use Diss and the Instant.

Bosses: 
- Anomalus, Rupturan and Chess: Dissolvent and Corrosive 2+1 depending on the spec.
- Medivh: Can be hurt with any kind of poisons, but you should be using Mind numbing if you are combat. Diss for Assa
- Every other boss can only be hurt with Deadly and instant. Combat and Sub uses Deadly 5+4, Assa uses Instant.

Edit: I tested it and it seems like they removed the inmunties on the worgens and the demons, making it a bit less of an issue.

author: Nelson
content:
i've tested this variation too, the extra point on slice is useless because you always go envenom -> slice 1cp, and they last for the same duration if u have 2 points on imp slice anyways, also hat is more reliable cuz it procs off ur crits too and it inst that hard to get a crit since by the time u cheap shot kidney ends u proc it at least twice which makes 2 of ur hemos "costs 30 energy", also serrated blades is useless in pvp, the difference is completely irrelevant, not having faster vanish and blind makes no sense to me and 10 energy cost on every cheap shot makes a huge difference, also ghostly strike is a buffed version of hemo in terms of dmg which increases ur speed and costs less energy, theres no reason to go serrated over it imo.

i get the idea but in terms of build path the prob with vigor is that u need to spend MORE points in assa that you will not get as much value in return, compared to hat that u get value out of every single point u spend in sub

ps. and the problem with vigor too was that in the tests that i did i realize that you start to get real value out of vigor when u have envenom up, while hat as soon as u cheap shot and u land a white swing crit or hemo you already get ur rotation smoother, i just felt like in realistic scenarios when you fighting ppl that actually hit you back and u need to be constantly reseting and playing around stunlocks hat worked out better, if you playing against bots in bgs and ppl dont hit u and u can perma have envenom slice uptime and just hemo ppl down like a warrior then vigor might be better
